text:
rohit: Heads up — noticed a recurring decode stall when structured outputs + function/tool calls hit the runtime. Batches pile up for ~60–120ms until the tool pause returns. Profiling attached briefly below.

eva: ugh. is this the stop-token race we saw before or something new?

rohit: looks slightly different. stop-token handling contributes but the bigger signal is kernel-switch thrash during pause/resume. When a request pauses for toolcall the kernel selection logic evicts some fused attention kernels and then the resumed request picks a slower fallback path.

lex: can you paste the perf numbers?

rohit: sure. rough from devbox run: total latency (no toolcall) 210ms p95, with toolcall pause 340ms p95. decode-only portion jumps from 120ms to 240ms on resumed path. KV cache hit rate unchanged. CPU scheduling looks fine.

rohit: stack snippet we logged:```[RESUME] seq=42 picked_kernel=attn_fused_opt_v2 fallback=attn_generic_v1 kv_cpy=false```

sara: kv_cpy=false means no KV copy but kernel mismatch still causes >extra kernel load latency. Could be JIT/kernel-cache warming.

lex: any quick mitigations? increase token budget thresholds or avoid kernel swap on resume?

eva: maybe we can keep the resumed request pinned to its previous exec path. Add resume_hint that forces same kernel selection if hardware+model match. cheap opt.

rohit: tried a resume_hint prototype: p95 dropped from 340ms->290ms. better but still noisy. The bigger delta is when batch formation mixes resumed short tail and fresh long sequences — kernel selector prefers different microkernels for different seq len distributions.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert: batch-shape variance correlated with 12% p95 tail increase in last deploy.

lex: Hmm. sounds like queue policy needs to handle resumed vs new requests separately. Maybe a two-queue system: resumed-first, new-late, or a small hold-window to coalesce similar seq-lens.

rohit: tried a small hold window (30ms) for resumed-only batches; that reduced kernel churn but increased avg latency by 6ms. p95 improved ~7%. tradeoff seems acceptable for SLAs.

sara: we should also consider token_budget tweaking: lower target tokens for resumed requests so they don't force kernel selection that favors long-context microkernels.

lex: config idea: resume_priority_queue=true; resume_hold_ms=30; resume_token_budget=16; kernel_hint_on_resume=sticky. Any objections?

eva: no objections. let's test across quantized models too — kernel variants differ more there.

rohit: will run cross-model CI on small fleet. quick repro script:```# repro loop
for i in range(100):
  call = gen_request(prompt, stop_token, call_tool=True)
  if i % 7 == 0:
    simulate_tool_pause(50ms)
  send(call)
```

lex: can you dump kernel-selection histograms for before/after? want to see swap frequency.

rohit: yes. initial glance shows swap freq down from 0.18->0.05 per-request with the sticky hint.

perf-bot: note: running rollout job 4832 against canary pool.

rohit: plan: 1) land resume_hint + resume_queue rules behind flag, 2) run cross-model perf CI, 3) measure p50/p95 and kernel-swap metric, 4) if stable, rollout canary.

lex: add an observability metric: kernel_swap_count per-request + kernel_warm_time so we can monitor regressions automatically.

rohit: will add both. Also putting a small emergency fallback: if resume_hold_ms causes p99 spikes for interactive tier, auto-disable for that tier.

eva: sounds good. Also add an eval set with structured-output prompts that exercise stop-token early termination and toolcall pauses. Keeps quality/regressions visible.

rohit: yep. tagging @sara for KV cache check: can we ensure no hidden copies happen on resume across certain devices?

sara: will audit memory paths tomorrow. initial hypothesis: on some GPUs quantized kernels require a reformat step that looks like a KV materialize; if we can keep format consistent on pause we avoid it.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: redwood-runtime/feat/resume-hint -> canary (pool: infra-canary-2)

rohit: thanks. I'll post a short follow-up with CI numbers and kernel histograms. if anyone wants to test earlier, flag is `--enable-resume-hint` in runtime binary.

lex: :thumbsup: thanks rohit.
